findings.why: _tail_hash cache is never invalidated; a Ledger that has already appended writes a stale prev_hash when another instance appends to the same file in between (A→B→A), silently breaking the FR-2 hash chain. AC-4 only tests two fresh instances and cannot catch this.
test_AC_STORY_01_05_5 mocks os.fsync and reads back in-process, so it never exercises the criterion's 'separate process' clause and asserts durability by mock-call rather than behavior.
no lock between tail read (_prev_hash) and append write; concurrent appenders read the same prev_hash and produce a hash-chain fork, breaking the single-chain integrity invariant

findings: [medium] ledgerlock/ledger.py:25 — `append` computes `prev_hash` (line 25 via `_prev_hash` reading the disk tail at line 47) with no file lock held between the tail read and the `open(..., "ab")` write at line 52: two processes appending concurrently to the same path both read the same tail (or both `GENESIS`), so both write lines with an identical `prev_hash`, producing a hash-chain fork that breaks the single-chain tamper-evidence invariant (`line[i].prev_hash == line[i-1].hash`) with no data-loss protection against it.
